messages.author: 2a5dcfbe2fdafe70
messages.subject: Periodicity From Fixed Station Telemetry
parts:
Hi Chris,

I reached out previously about a set of telemetry data for bats that I used to get spatial location estimates using the 'razimuth' package created by Gerber et al., 2018.

I then followed methodology from Rizzuto et al., 2021 to incorporate the error estimates into ctmm. I successfully incorporated the error estimates using your uere() fix.

I am looking to incorporate periodicity into these models. The data were collected on bats during the maternity season that are returning to a nightly roost and data was only collected at night. I recognize there are some issues with the sampling regime overlapping with the periodic behavior and I have some additional data that records them as present or absent at the roost every 30 minutes that I am hoping to also incorporate.

I have an example of three individuals and I am trying to understand which terms I should set for the periodograms as well as if dropping error improves the model fit due to decreased number of parameters. Both the error and non-error currently have a period of 24 hours and circle=FALSE.

Thank you for your help!


Best,

Amber Litterer

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Periodicity From Fixed Station Telemetry
parts:
Hi Amber,

If the error model is good, then dropping it won't improve the fit, as it's conditioning on extra data. Dropping it will only speed up the computation.
The gaps shouldn't be a problem for the model fits, but will show up in the periodogram.

Best,
Chris
